description: Unmodified local copies for design study, grouped by what each image supports. These are historical references, not a new live-site audit.

images.study: Large editorial type paired with plain supporting text; an object scene creates a second visual focus. Warm surrounding surfaces leave room for the content.
images.boundary: Study type roles and composition. Do not require this font, copy, hero height, background texture, or object network in another project.

images.study: The same editorial/object relationship survives a dark treatment. Neutral surroundings let the forms retain their material detail.
images.boundary: The assistant bubble overlaps content in this capture; its placement is not endorsed. Dark mode is a project decision.

images.study: A quiet project frame gives the artifact most of the space. Plain project type, restrained metadata, and clear actions support the image.
images.boundary: The cover is identified as generated in the captured site. Treat it as presentation, not documentary proof of real-world use.

images.study: Dark chrome preserves the original light media rather than recoloring the project artifact. The surrounding frame stays consistent.
images.boundary: Do not inherit every fixed control or assume a dark page requires darkening product screenshots.

images.study: Large project imagery carries distinct identities inside a common index. Compact view controls offer a visible way to change browsing mode.
images.boundary: Card count, masonry arrangement, moving copy, and fixed filter position are site-specific. Use a stable summary in future listings.

images.study: The compact index uses thumbnails, names, metadata, and short summaries for scanning on a small screen.
images.boundary: Use its scan hierarchy only when a collection needs it. Do not copy the number of modes or the amount of opening chrome.

images.study: A before-and-after comparison is paired with the question, choice, and instructions for reading the screen.
images.boundary: The adjacent slide is partly visible and fixed tools remain present. Extract the evidence-and-explanation relationship, not the clipping or overlay.

images.study: The evidence and its captions stack into a readable sequence. Controls expose the selected slide and available next step.
images.boundary: Tiny text inside the original slide still needs the text alternative and original-size route. A photograph or screenshot alone cannot prove a usability outcome.

images.study: One project image relates phone, kiosk, and vehicle touchpoints. The shared narrative frame can hold a different service identity.
images.boundary: This is a browser adaptation of a service concept. Its purple and dark screens are project-specific, not universal palette preferences.

images.study: Financial information and a consumer widget retain their own blue identity inside the neutral portfolio shell.
images.boundary: Use the domain-specific information structure as context. Do not copy dashboard numbers, brand assets, or make claims about private functionality.

images.study: A photograph shows the performer, instrument, and acoustic machine in the same scene. The subject supplies the strong color.
images.boundary: Stage lighting is content, not a default purple UI theme. Keep photography credits when using it publicly.

images.study: The tablet, spatial layers, wires, and lights make the relationship between input and represented computation visible.
images.boundary: A still image demonstrates physical arrangement, not recognition accuracy, timing, or visitor comprehension. Photo attribution must be checked before publication.

images.study: Visible servos, wiring, picks, strings, and wood communicate how the object is built. Craft includes the mechanism, not only the finished enclosure.
images.boundary: Use it to study material and mechanism legibility. It is not a prompt to decorate unrelated UI with exposed wires or wooden textures.

images.study: The specimen has its own graphic composition and color; the portfolio frame remains recognizable.
images.boundary: The purple cover belongs to this artifact. The typeface is a display study, not a required body or UI font.

images.study: Angle, vertical, and linear cuts form a repeated construction idea across different letterforms. Large specimens make the detail inspectable.
images.boundary: The artifact includes its original copy and layout. Study consistency of construction without reproducing its writing or treating this font as a general UI choice.

images.study: A knife and carved surface connect the visual idea to a specific material gesture. The reference explains why the letterform intervention exists.
images.boundary: The embedded inspiration photography has its own attribution requirements. Use this as a record of the project’s references, not as a licensed stock asset.

images.study: The archive metaphor has a complete visual setting, object language, and tone of voice. Play grows from the subject.
images.boundary: The inscription text is too small and subdued to use as a legibility reference. Preserve the coherent idea while improving essential reading.

images.study: The same archive changes its atmosphere from day to night, showing how a coherent concept can support expressive theme variation.
images.boundary: Use for atmosphere only. The captured title and metadata have readability concerns; do not copy their low contrast.

images.study: The intended hierarchy pairs editorial headings with small labels, project links, and an object illustration for each idea.
images.boundary: This capture followed category navigation because direct entry was broken. The image is useful for intended hierarchy, not evidence that route loading is correct.

images.study: The earlier screen lets a reader identify the dominance of device information and the division between active and inactive apps.
images.boundary: This is comparison evidence, not a recommended starting style. It does not establish the results of testing.

images.study: The later screen gives app launching more space and consolidates the device area. Compare it with V20 to see the hierarchy change.
images.boundary: Transfer the prioritization decision when relevant, not the icon artwork, shadows, exact layout, or implied release status.

images.study: A large reserved scene area pushes the introduction down on a 390px-wide screen.
images.boundary: Use as a spacing counterexample. Preserve expressive form while bringing the task and content into a stronger relationship.

images.study: Direct-entry styling failed in this capture, leaving navigation over the heading and compressing the content hierarchy.
images.boundary: Do not copy the small title, unstyled links, or overlap. V19 records the intended hierarchy after the missing styles loaded.

images.study: The full specimen splits weight names within words and has a lower navigation surface over the specimen area.
images.boundary: Keep functional labels intact and protect editable content from persistent controls. The typeface concept itself remains a positive reference.
